title: E-Math algebra: expansion, factorisation and changing the subject
subject: math

objectives.text: Expand brackets using the area model
successCriteria: I can expand (x + 3)(x + 2) into three terms using the tiles
I can say where each term in the expansion comes from
assessmentPoints: Board answers during the area-model walkthrough
First drill set in the closing activity

successCriteria: I can group 2x + 6 + xy + 3y into pairs and take out the common factors
I can check a factorisation by expanding it back
assessmentPoints: Pair answers in the grouping activity

objectives.text: Change the subject of a formula by undoing operations in reverse
successCriteria: I can make x the subject of y = 3x + 5
I can state the inverse operation at each step
assessmentPoints: Step-by-step class responses during the worked example

objectives.text: Explain why (a + b)^2 has three terms, not two
successCriteria: I can expand (a + b)^2 and name the middle term 2ab
I can explain why a^2 + b^2 is too small
assessmentPoints: Responses when the trap is sprung
Closing drill answers on the trap variant

differentiation.support: Colour-code the two pairs before taking out the common factors.

differentiation.stretch: Ask pairs to find the error in (x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 25 in one line.
